main_issue: Whether Agent D can keep showering and cooking at 4:45 a.m. every morning despite waking the others, or must shift the noise to the night before

A-B.evidence: Both state noise-related needs (A's Monday presentations, B's exams, turns 3-4); neither addresses the other. Both ask D for night-before accommodation (turns 6, 9).

A-C.evidence: Both are bothered by D's early noise (turns 1, 3, 12, 18) but never address each other.

A-D.evidence: A asks for Sunday-night prep (turn 6); D agrees: 'For Sunday nights, I can do that. I'll shower the night before' (turn 7); A thanks D (turn 8).

B-C.evidence: Both object to the noise (B turns 4, 9; C turns 12, 18) but never address each other.

B-D.evidence: B asks for night-before showering on Monday/Wednesday (turn 9) and then only Wednesday (turn 11); D refuses: 'I can't also give up my shower' (turn 10), and 'can't give it up more than the one night' (turn 13).

C-D.evidence: C: 'It will wake me up every day' (turn 18); then C asks D to shower quickly with no hairdryer (turn 23) and D agrees (turn 27); C thanks D (turns 28, 31) but the 4:45 shower stays.
